name: list-order-reverts-after-two-quick-moves
justification: The tempting alternative is test_code: the message names a locator and a timeout, which is the signature of a spec that asserted before the page settled. It is not one. The spec counts the write responses and only makes its final assertion once both have arrived, so nothing was in flight when the wait began; every step is a web-first assertion and there is no fixed wait anywhere in the file. The wait expired because the rendered order never converged. The client applies whichever reorder response arrives last rather than whichever reorder was issued last, so a slow first response silently reverts the second — the stored rows hold both moves while the list shows one, and a reload corrects the display. Rule 2 does not fire because the test encodes no unsafe assumption, so rule 3 decides and the product is what is implicated. Intermittent because the last five runs contain passes: 9 failures in 20 runs, alternating.
